subject: Telehealth streaming transcription — PHI handling & BAA scope
messages:
From: Jackson Lee <jackson.lee@mercuryhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telehealth streaming transcription - PHI handling & BAA question

Hi Naomi,

Quick one from our security team as we evaluate Redwood for live telehealth transcription: we plan to stream audio from our telehealth app to Redwood for real-time transcription and optional post-call indexing. A couple of clarifying questions before we move to a security review: 

- Does Redwood consider live audio and the resulting transcripts PHI under HIPAA when tied to patient identifiers?
- Can we get a BAA that explicitly covers streaming ingestion and short-term transcript storage?
- What are the default retention and log policies for streaming sessions (audio, transcript, metadata)?
- Do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest for transcripts?

Our security team also asked for: a simple dataflow diagram, SOC 2 evidence (summary or report), and an estimated timeline to execute a BAA.

Can you point me to the right folks/answers?

Thanks,
Jackson
Jackson Lee
Head of Security Engineering
Mercury Telehealth
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jackson Lee <jackson.lee@mercuryhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telehealth streaming transcription - PHI handling & BAA question

Jackson — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Dev (serving/runtime) and Evelyn (product/BAA owner) to confirm technical limits and the paperwork timeline. High-level answers below; see attachments for a diagram and a draft BAA we typically start from.

- PHI classification: Yes — if audio or transcripts are tied to identifiers (name, MRN, persistent user IDs), we treat that as PHI and recommend a BAA. Redwood’s policy is to classify on ingestion: if a customer indicates PHI, we enable BAA protections and specific processing rules.

- BAA coverage: We can provide a standard BAA that explicitly names streaming ingestion, transient transcript storage, and telemetry required for debugging. We also offer an addendum for Dedicated and Private deployments that tightens scope (no multi-tenant storage, separate logs). Draft attached: redwood-draft-baa-v1.pdf

- Retention defaults: For hosted (multi-tenant) deployments the default transient transcript retention is 30 days; for Dedicated/Private we can set retention to customer-defined values (including ephemeral retention like 0-24 hours). We can also offer auto-purge hooks and configurable redaction.

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we support envelope encryption with BYOK options in enterprise plans.

Next steps we recommend:
1) You share a short dataflow (if different from our attached diagram) and example session metadata fields you need preserved.
2) Tell us if you require Dedicated or Private — that changes BAA language/timeline.
3) We provide the SOC 2 summary and a DocuSign link for the BAA.

Dev / Evelyn — can you confirm whether we can offer a 24-hour ephemeral retention profile for streaming transcripts on Dedicated, and whether access logs for those sessions can be isolated per-customer?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
On Thu, Oct 4, 2028 at 11:05 AM Jackson Lee <jackson.lee@mercuryhealth.com> wrote:
> Naomi — thanks, that helps a lot. A few clarifications from our side: 
> 
> - We absolutely require a BAA. Preferred deployment is hosted Dedicated (reserved pool) but if there are data residency or isolation gaps we may need Private.
> - Retention: our compliance team wants transcripts to be ephemeral by default (24 hours) and only persisted longer if explicitly requested by a clinician. Can you confirm the auto-purge API or webhook workflow?
> - Logging: we need audit logs that show which Redwood principal (service account) accessed a transcript, and we need exportable logs for e-discovery with retention of 7 years (we realize this is long — we may choose to export and store logs in our own S3 behind our retention policies).
> 
> Finally, can you share a SOC 2 Type II report summary and any gap notes around controlled access to ephemeral media? We will include the SOC 2 summary in our vendor review.
> 
> Jackson
>
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jackson Lee <jackson.lee@mercuryhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Oct 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telehealth streaming transcription - PHI handling & BAA question

Jackson — following up with specifics after internal confirmation. Summary + attachments included.

- Ephemeral retention: Confirmed. For Dedicated and Private we can offer a 24-hour ephemeral retention profile for streaming transcripts. We expose an auto-purge webhook and an API to mark sessions as "persist" for clinician-approved retention. We will supply the webhook spec in the onboarding doc.

- Audit logs: We will produce per-customer audit logs that include: timestamp, Redwood service principal, API key id, session id, action (read/write/purge), and actor IP. Logs can be exported to your S3 via an encrypted delivery pipeline or streamed in near-real-time to your SIEM. For long-term legal retention (7 years) we recommend exporting logs to your account; Redwood will retain a configurable window (default 90 days for Dedicated unless otherwise contracted).

- KMS & encryption: Customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated/Private. For hosted Dedicated we can enable BYOK and use a scoped key for transcript objects.

- SOC 2: See attached soc2-summary-2028.pdf. For the full report we can run an NDA route; we include the summary on our vendor portal link if you need immediate review.

- BAA timeline: If you accept standard language, typical execution is 3-5 business days once the DocuSign is returned. If you require Private deployment or additional controls, timeline can be 2-4 weeks (ops & procurement coordination). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234

Attachments included: redwood-draft-baa-v1.pdf (BAA draft), telehealth-dataflow-20281004.png (dataflow), soc2-summary-2028.pdf (SOC2 summary).
